upwork-vibe~upwork-job-scraper.title: Custom Nonprofit CRM & Database System — Full Stack Developer
upwork-vibe~upwork-job-scraper.description:
ABOUT US
We are a small nonprofit organization seeking to replace our current CRM (Neon CRM) with a fully custom, open-source solution. We need a system that is intuitive for a non-technical team, flexible enough to grow with our organization, and built on open-source technology to keep costs low. We have prior experience with a custom SQL-based system paired with a front-facing web interface and are confident this approach suits our needs.

WHAT WE NEED BUILT
- Donor management & nurturing: donor profiles, giving history, communication logs, segmentation, and automated outreach sequences
- Donation tracking: one-time and recurring donations, receipting, reporting, and payment gateway integration
- Grant management: application intake, staff review/approval workflows, deadline tracking, and funder records
- Program management: participant tracking, outcomes reporting, and program-level dashboards
- Volunteer management: opportunity listings, sign-up, hours tracking, and communication
- Email & newsletter tools: list management, template builder, scheduled sends, and open/click tracking
- Calendar: team-facing event and deadline management integrated with the rest of the system; member specific calendar with upcoming events
- Workflow automation: configurable triggers for reminders, follow-ups, task assignments, and status changes
- Reporting & dashboards: exportable reports across all modules with visual summaries for leadership

TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS
IMPORTANT: Must be open-source stack. No proprietary SaaS platforms. Self-hostable.

- Open-source relational database (PostgreSQL preferred)
- Modern web framework for the front-end interface (React, Vue, or similar)
- RESTful or GraphQL API backend
- Role-based access control with staff permission levels
- Responsive design — usable on desktop and tablet
- Data migration from Neon CRM (we will provide export files)
- Hosted on a VPS or cloud provider (open to discussion)
- Clean documentation and handoff so we are not permanently dependent on one developer

REQUIRED SKILLS
PostgreSQL/MySQL, React or Vue.js, Node.js or Python, REST API design, Authentication/RBAC, Data migration, Linux/VPS hosting, UI/UX for non-technical users

NICE TO HAVE
Nonprofit sector experience, CRM development, Email API integration (SendGrid etc.), Payment gateway integration, Docker/CI-CD, familiarity with open-source CRM tools

WHAT TO INCLUDE IN YOUR PROPOSAL
1. Links to similar projects — especially nonprofit, CRM, or custom database work
2. Your recommended tech stack and a brief explanation of why
3. How you would approach the data migration from Neon CRM
4. Estimated timeline broken into phases (discovery, build, testing, launch)
5. Your rate and preferred payment structure (fixed or hourly)
6. How you handle documentation and handoff at project end

A NOTE FROM US
We are a small, non-technical team counting on you to guide us through decisions about stack and architecture. We want a long-term partner, not just someone to build and disappear. Strong communication, honest timelines, and a willingness to explain things clearly matter as much as technical skill. We are open to starting with a paid discovery phase to properly scope the project.

8. **Two-column USP block** – two premium tiles with photo backgrounds + CTA
9. **ProvenExpert strip** – logo, score, 3 testimonials

Product/category/customer migration, payment providers, shipping/tax/legal pages, ERP integration, multi-language, SEO meta, blog, photography, copy, brand assets.

2. `README.md`: install, build, enable, list of overridden blocks, list of `theme.json` fields.
3. One demo install (your dev server or ours) showing the 11 sections with placeholder content.

### Working with us

English only. Async by default. Up to two 45-min calls (kickoff + mid-review); extras at your hourly rate. We respond within 1 business day, CET. Mockup is image-only — **no Figma file**.

upwork-vibe~upwork-job-scraper.description:
Overview
We're a small real estate development company running a suite of internal web tools to manage construction loan draw packages, budget tracking, invoice intake, and bank reconciliation across ~ multiple active properties. The tools are currently built as single-file HTML apps (React via CDN, no build step) deployed on Netlify, using Dropbox as a makeshift data store (JSON files). We need to replace Dropbox with a proper database backend before we scale further.
This is a focused backend/infrastructure job — we are NOT looking for a frontend rewrite.

Current Data Model
The database will need to support the following entities:

Properties - active projects (name, address, loan details)
Invoices - vendor, amount, date, CSI division, status, linked PDF, linked property
Draw Packages - grouping of invoices submitted to the bank for reimbursement; draw number, date, status, total
Draw Line Items - individual invoice allocations within a draw package
Budget - per property, per CSI division (18 divisions, ~100 line items); original budget, revised budget, invoiced to date
Bank Transactions - imported from CSV bank statements; matchable to one or more invoices
Reconciliation Records - matched pairs between bank transactions and invoices, with match status and notes
Users - internal users only; no public access, no self-registration


Tech Preferences
Our strong preference is Supabase (hosted PostgreSQL + REST API + Auth). If you have a strong reason to propose an alternative (e.g. Railway + raw PostgreSQL + Node API), we're open — but please justify it. We are not interested in Firebase, MongoDB, or other document stores.

Deliverables

Schema design document — table definitions, relationships, indexes, and rationale for key decisions. To be reviewed and approved before build begins.
Supabase project setup — tables, foreign keys, RLS (Row Level Security) policies for our 2 users, and any necessary functions/triggers.
Data migration — existing Dropbox JSON files (we'll provide exports) migrated cleanly into the new schema.
JavaScript client module — a thin wrapper around the Supabase client covering CRUD for each entity, to replace our existing Dropbox read/write calls across all apps.
Basic documentation — how to add a new property, how to run migrations if we add fields, connection details.


What We're Not Looking For

A frontend rewrite
A new UI or admin dashboard
An ongoing retainer
Someone unavailable after handoff — we need 2–3 weeks of post-delivery support for integration questions


Ideal Candidate

Strong PostgreSQL schema design experience
Hands-on Supabase experience including RLS policies
Comfortable reading existing vanilla JS / React UMD code
Bonus: familiarity with construction draw or AIA billing workflows

upwork-vibe~upwork-job-scraper.title: Migrate static brand-hub web app (Created via Claude) to Supabase backend and publish to our url
upwork-vibe~upwork-job-scraper.description:
## Project type

Fixed price

## Estimated budget

open to proposals — please justify your number

## Experience level

Intermediate

---

## Project description

We're a small Danish ecommerce brand wanting a custom-built **brand-hub / DAM** as a static website. It's already fully featured — searchable asset library, brand book editor, collections, folders, role-based access, multi-language UI (EN/DA), multi-select downloads, brand book PDF export, etc. The full source is on GitHub and we'll share it with you privately on day one.

The hub currently stores everything in the browser (localStorage + IndexedDB), which works but means no cross-device sync, no real password reset, and no server-side audit log. **We want to keep the entire frontend exactly as it is and only swap the storage layer to a real backend.**

The codebase was deliberately architected for this migration. All storage flows through two thin files: `js/store.js` (metadata) and `js/idb.js` (file blobs). The function signatures are stable — your job is to write Supabase-backed implementations of those signatures. The UI (`app.js`, `admin.js`, brand book renderer) should not need any changes.

We've already written a detailed migration plan with schema sketches and code skeletons. You'll find it at `docs/PRODUCTION-MIGRATION.md` in the repo.

## Scope of work

1. **Set up a Supabase project** (we'll create the account, you'll configure it)
   - Create database schema for: assets, collections, folders, invite codes, requests, comments, activity log, brand book, appearance, home settings, upload rules.
   - Create a Storage bucket for file blobs.
   - Configure Row-Level Security so admins / team / viewer / invite-code-guest each see only what they should.
   - Configure Auth: email/password + password reset emails.

2. **Swap the frontend storage layer**
   - Rewrite `js/store.js` to call the Supabase JS SDK instead of localStorage. Keep the public interface identical (see `js/store.js` head of file for the current function list).
   - Rewrite `js/idb.js` to upload/download from Supabase Storage instead of IndexedDB. Keep the `idb: id` reference format so the existing render code continues to work.

upwork-vibe~upwork-job-scraper.description:
We are a growing business and need help properly rebuilding and structuring our accounting and inventory systems for scalability and operational accuracy as we migrate to a different ERP system.
---

# Current Software Stack

## Current Systems
* QuickBooks Online
* DigitBridge ERP

## New System
* SOS Inventory
* QuickBooks Online
---

# Core Problem

Our current ERP (DigitBridge) only syncs summarized sales transaction totals into QuickBooks Online.

QuickBooks DOES NOT contain:
* item-level invoice history
* detailed SKU-level sales history
* detailed historical inventory movement

Instead, QuickBooks mainly contains summarized accounting transaction data.

This means:

* QuickBooks is NOT our historical source of truth for inventory/sales detail
* DigitBridge contains much of the detailed operational/item-level data
* We need to preserve and migrate historical operational data correctly into SOS Inventory
---

# Additional Historical Data Complexity

In the past, our team manually entered invoices into SOS Inventory in order to preserve item-level sales history and operational data.

As a result:

* some historical data exists in DigitBridge
* some historical invoice/item-level data exists in SOS Inventory
* QuickBooks primarily contains summarized accounting transaction data

This means our historical data currently exists across multiple systems with possible:
* overlap
* duplication
* inconsistencies
* inventory reconciliation issues

We need someone who can:
* evaluate the current state of the data
* identify duplicate/conflicting records
* determine the best source of truth for different data types
* preserve inventory and reporting integrity
* avoid duplicate sales/inventory history during migration
* establish clean operational workflows moving forward
---

# Important Technical Details

SOS Inventory allows CSV imports for:

* Items
* Customers
* Vendors
* BOMs
* Price tiers
* Sales orders
* Sales receipts

However:

* SOS Inventory does NOT support invoice imports
* Syncing QuickBooks into SOS Inventory only transfers summarized sales totals, NOT itemized invoice detail

We need help determining the BEST strategy for:

* preserving historical inventory and sales data
* rebuilding inventory accuracy moving forward
* structuring QuickBooks + SOS Inventory properly
* creating clean operational workflows moving forward
---

# What We Need Help With

## 1. ERP + Data Migration Strategy

We need guidance on:
* best practices for migrating historical data
* how much historical data should actually be migrated
* preserving inventory valuation and reporting integrity
* preventing duplicate or corrupted transactional data
* determining the best system/source of truth moving forward
---

## 2. DigitBridge Data Extraction + Migration

We need help:
* extracting historical item-level sales/inventory data from DigitBridge
* mapping/exporting data into usable CSV format(s)
* importing supported data into SOS Inventory
* cleaning SKU/item data if necessary
* validating migrated inventory accuracy
---

## 3. QuickBooks Cleanup & Proper Structure

We want to:
* clean up and properly structure QuickBooks Online
* build a clean and scalable Chart of Accounts
* properly structure inventory accounting workflows
* improve reporting accuracy moving forward

We care more about creating a scalable and accurate operational system moving forward than trying to perfectly reconstruct years of historical bookkeeping.
---

## 4. SOS Inventory Setup

We need assistance with:
* SOS Inventory implementation
* QuickBooks Online integration
* inventory workflows
* purchasing workflows
* sales order workflows
* warehouse/inventory best practices
* reporting structure
---

# Ideal Freelancer Qualifications

We are specifically looking for someone experienced with:
* QuickBooks Online
* SOS Inventory
* ERP migrations
* Inventory accounting
* Distribution / wholesale businesses
* SKU and inventory management
* Historical inventory migrations
* CSV mapping/imports
* Operational accounting systems
* Data reconciliation

BONUS if you have experience with:
* DigitBridge
* warehouse/distribution operations
* ecommerce integrations
* inventory-heavy businesses
---

# What Success Looks Like
We want:
* a clean and scalable QuickBooks structure
* accurate inventory workflows moving forward
* successful migration from DigitBridge to SOS Inventory
* preserved historical operational data where practical
* accurate reporting and inventory visibility
* operational processes that scale as the business grows

---

# Please Include In Your Proposal
1. Your experience with ERP + inventory migrations
2. Your recommended migration strategy based on the details above
3. Estimated timeline and budget range

Pipedrive CRM Setup, Automation, and Lead Import Expert (Heavy Equipment Brokerage)
 
We are a heavy equipment brokerage (www.bigassmotors.com) that utilizes a speculative sourcing model. We post representative machinery listings online, syndicate them to industrial advertising sites (like Machinio), and receive highly targeted, warm lead inquiries on what buyers are looking to purchase.

We need a certified Pipedrive CRM expert to architect a clean, visual workspace from scratch. You will design our sales pipeline, configure custom equipment-specific data fields, import our existing spreadsheet lead lists, and set up automated lead ingestion so that inbound listing leads instantly populate our pipeline.

Scope of Work & Key Deliverables

Custom Pipeline & Stage Design:

Configure our primary, visual "First Call to Close" drag-and-drop Kanban pipeline.

Pipeline stages will include: Inbound Inquiry ➔ Discovery Call ➔ Sourcing Match ➔ Under Contract ➔ Escrow/Diligence ➔ Logistics/Dispatch ➔ Deal Closed.

Heavy Equipment Custom Fields:

Design and implement custom fields to standardize our equipment profiles.

Custom fields must include: Target Machinery Class (dropdown), Maximum Operating Hours (numeric), Target Budget (monetary), Serial Number (text), Inspection Status (dropdown), and Buyer Shipping Location (text).

Data Migration & Spreadsheet Import:

Review, clean, and map our existing lead spreadsheet lists.

Import our historical contact database directly into Pipedrive, ensuring clean matching to "People" and "Organizations" without creating duplicate records.

Automated Lead Ingestion:

Configure a workflow (using webhooks, Zapier, or Pipedrive’s native email/API parser) that triggers the moment we receive a lead notification from Machinio.

The automation must instantly parse the email/data body (extracting the buyer's contact info, specific machine sought, and budget limits) and auto-create a new "Deal" card in our Inbound Inquiry pipeline stage.

Workflow Automations & Reminders:

Set up automated follow-up tasks and activity reminders for our sales reps when a deal sits too long in a specific stage.

Set up an automated client notification sequence (via synced email templates) once a deal enters the "Under Contract" stage.


Automation Mastery: Advanced experience with Zapier, webhook creation, and Pipedrive API integrations.

Data Migration Skills: Expert-level knowledge of Excel/CSV data cleaning and structured importing into Pipedrive databases.

Industry Familiarity (Bonus): Prior experience setting up CRMs for commercial automotive, logistics, real estate, or industrial equipment sectors.

Project Details
Project Type: One-time project with potential for ongoing monthly maintenance/optimization.

Duration: Estimated 1 to 2 weeks.

Budget: Please provide a fixed-price proposal based on the deliverables above, or your hourly rate.

upwork-vibe~upwork-job-scraper.title: System Migration from JTL-Wawi to Odoo (Implementation & Training)
upwork-vibe~upwork-job-scraper.description:
German-speaking applicants are preferred.

Project Description: System Migration from JTL-Wawi to Odoo (Implementation & Training)
1. Background & Objective
We are currently using JTL-Wawi as our inventory management and order fulfillment system. To future-proof our business and consolidate our processes, we are migrating our entire ERP infrastructure to Odoo (preferably Odoo.sh or Odoo Online).

We are looking for an experienced Odoo Consultant or Partner Agency to handle this project as a turnkey solution ("do-it-for-me") and to provide comprehensive hands-on training for our team.

2. Scope of Work
Phase 1: Process Analysis & System Setup
Analyze our current JTL workflows (Purchasing, Sales, Inventory, Accounting).

Configure the Odoo database (selecting the required apps, setting up number ranges, invoice layouts, and German localization/tax settings).

Phase 2: Data Migration (JTL ➔ Odoo)
Clean, map, and fully import master data from the JTL database into Odoo:

Product Master Data (including complex variant structures, descriptions, prices, and barcodes).

Customer & Vendor Data (including address history).

Optional: Import of historical order data (to be discussed).

Transfer initial inventory levels on the cutoff date.

Phase 3: Integrations & Multichannel Setup
Connect our existing sales channels (e.g., online shop, marketplaces) to Odoo.

Set up payment gateways (e.g., PayPal, Stripe, bank synchronization via FinTS/Ponto).

Integrate shipping carriers (e.g., DHL, DPD).

Phase 4: Training & Enablement
Provide practical, hands-on training sessions in a staging/sandbox environment using our actual migrated data.

Focus areas: Order processing, purchasing, stock management, invoicing, and month-end closing processes.

Phase 5: Go-Live & Hypercare
Support and monitor the final system switch (Go-Live over a weekend / specific cutoff date).

Provide dedicated support immediately after launch to resolve user questions or system tweaks.

3. Requirements for the Contractor
Proven track record of successful Odoo implementations (preferably Version 17/18).

Understanding of JTL-Wawi is a massive advantage to quickly grasp our current data structures and workflows.

Fluent communication in German is highly preferred for the training sessions.

Hands-on mindset: We need someone who manages the technical execution entirely while guiding us through the transition seamlessly.

Aktuell nutzen wir JTL-Wawi für unsere Warenwirtschaft und Auftragsabwicklung. Wir möchten unser ERP-System zukunftssicher aufstellen und vollständig auf Odoo (bevorzugt Odoo.sh oder Odoo Online) umsteigen.

Gesucht wird ein erfahrener Odoo-Consultant oder eine Partner-Agentur, die dieses Projekt schlüsselfertig für uns umsetzt ("Do-it-for-me") und uns intensiv im Umgang mit dem neuen System schult.

Phase 1: Prozessanalyse & System-Setup
Analyse unserer aktuellen JTL-Workflows (Einkauf, Verkauf, Lager, Rechnungswesen).

Konfiguration der Odoo-Datenbank (Auswahl der passenden Apps, Einrichtung von Nummernkreisen, Rechnungs-Layouts und Steuereinstellungen für Deutschland).

Phase 2: Datenmigration (JTL ➔ Odoo)
Bereinigung, Mapping und vollständiger Import der Stammdaten aus der JTL-Datenbank:

Artikelstammdaten (inkl. komplexer Variantenstrukturen, Beschreibungen, Preise und Barcodes).

Kundendaten / Lieferantendaten (inkl. Adresshistorie).

Optional: Import von historischen Bestelldaten (nach Absprache).

Übertrag der initialen Lagerbestände zum Stichtag.

Phase 3: Schnittstellen & Multichannel-Anbindung
Anbindung unserer bestehenden Verkaufskanäle (z. B. Onlineshop, Marktplätze) an Odoo.

Einrichtung der Zahlungsanbieter (z. B. PayPal, Stripe, Bank-Synchronisation via FinTS/Ponto).

Anbindung von Versanddienstleistern (z. B. DHL, DPD).

Phase 4: Schulung & "Train the Trainer"
Praxisnahe Schulung der Geschäftsführung / Kern-Mitarbeiter direkt im Odoo-Testsystem (Sandbox) anhand unserer echten migrierten Daten.

Schwerpunkte: Auftragsschonung, Einkauf, Wareneingang, Lagerführung, Rechnungsstellung und Monatsabschluss.

Phase 5: Go-Live & Hypercare
Begleitung des finalen System-Wechsels (Go-Live am Wochenende / Stichtag).

Kurzfristiger Support direkt nach dem Livegang zur Behebung eventueller Anwenderfragen oder Systemfehler.

upwork-vibe~upwork-job-scraper.title: Professional Magento 2 Upgrade - 2.4.2 to v2.4.8 - Pristine clean Rebuild & Selective Data Migration

🛑 IMPORTANT NOTES: PROFESSIONALS ONLY

We are looking for a highly skilled Adobe Commerce (Magento 2) Solutions Architect/Developer to execute a clean-start rebuild of our e-commerce platform and build a robust, optimized, scalable, and production-ready environment.

This is a fixed-price project intended strictly for experienced professionals who genuinely understand and respect fixed-scope collaboration. The project structure, scope, and budget were carefully planned to support a serious, fair, and professional collaboration for both sides.

Job Description:

We are currently operating an established and fully functional Magento 2 e-commerce store running on Magento version 2.4.2. Our objective is to move the platform to Magento 2.4.8 with PHP 8.3.

This is not a brand-new website build.
The store already exists, including its design, structure, workflows, and core business functionalities. The goal is to professionally rebuild and remount the existing store inside a completely clean and optimized environment while preserving the current frontend experience and operational logic.

Instead of performing a traditional in-place upgrade — which typically carries over years of database clutter, unused modules, legacy configurations, hidden conflicts, and potentially malicious or unstable code — we have intentionally chosen a clean-environment rebuild strategy.

The project approach is simple:

Create a fresh Magento 2.4.8 installation on a clean server environment
Preserve the current design, structure, and functionality of the existing store
Migrate only the necessary and active relational data
Reinstall and configure extensions, services, and components that are required.
Eliminate accumulated technical debt by rebuilding correctly rather than attempting risky cleanup work inside the old environment.

The objective is to obtain a stable, lightweight, secure, and highly optimized Magento installation without inherited background issues, hidden loops, memory leaks, or obsolete configurations.

This should not be viewed as a “repair” project, but rather as a professional reconstruction using best practices and modern standards.

For an experienced Magento professional, this should be a straightforward and enjoyable project to execute, especially because everything will be built inside a fresh, controlled, and secure environment from the ground up.

Technical Roadmap & Project Scope:
STEP 1: Fresh Baseline & Clean Magento 2.4.8 Installation

Technical Execution: Set up a completely isolated, clean database and environment on the new staging directory. Install a pristine baseline of Magento 2.4.8 core cleanly via Composer. Do not copy, migrate, or reuse any existing core files from the old server setup.

Core Optimization & Regional Clean-up: We sell exclusively to customers in Romania and Europe. To make the platform as lightweight as possible, please disable the default Magento core modules and background loops that strictly target the American or Asian market infrastructures. This includes: Vertex, Amazon Pay, Braintree/PayPal core modules (non-European configurations), Yotpo, Dotdigital, and default US/Global Shipping Carriers. Identify and disable any other default core modules that strictly target non-European configurations.

STEP 2: Core Server Engines & Caching Stack Infrastructure

Install and configure separate, dedicated Redis instances (one for backend session handling, one for default application caching).

Install OpenSearch 2.x and map it as the primary catalog search engine.

Install and configure Varnish for Full Page Cache (FPC).

Critical: Varnish must be completely bypassed / turned OFF during the entire development and configuration phase.

STEP 3: Official Theme Installation & Visual Brand Alignment

Perform a 100% clean installation of the official MGS Claue (Parent) theme, followed by our customized Child Theme. Strict Rebranding Rule: Rename the child theme folder to "deepinvogue" and ensure all text fields and store names in the configuration reflect DeepInVogue. No code logic changes should be made to the theme files.

STEP 4: Native Magento Dual-Store Architecture Setup

Create a clean, dual-store view hierarchy under the main website bucket:

Store View 1: Romania (Base Currency: RON / Default Language: RO).

Store View 2: International (Base Currency: EUR / Default Language: EN).

Critical: Store codes and structural IDs must match our original live site exactly to maintain GTM/Facebook CAPI data integrity.

STEP 5: Core Extensions Installation & PHP 8.3 Compatibility Audit

Deploy operational extensions (GeoIP Store Switcher, Currency Switcher, Infinite Scroll, One Step Checkout, PayU Payment Gateway, Discount Module). Audit each for 100% stable execution under PHP 8.3. Run full compilation and static content deployment; monitor terminal logs for any PHP 8.3 deprecation notices or layout XML conflicts.

STEP 6: Extension Configuration & Checkout Optimization Strategy

Replicate exact configuration paths from our live site for extensions. Configure currency automated cron jobs. Replicate our simplified, fields-reduced checkout setup exactly; this requires our close, mutual consultation.

STEP 7: Relational Data Migration (The Clean Database Principle)

Perform highly selective, isolated relational data migration from the old database into our fresh, clean Magento 2.4.x structure, maintaining perfect relational integrity for:

Customers & Customer Groups.

Order History, Invoices, & Shipments.

Critical: Relational keys must remain perfectly intact.

STEP 8: Filtered Product Catalog & Clean Media Asset Import

Filter product catalog to include ONLY active, in-stock products.

Critical Media Rule: Migrate and map ONLY the images belonging to active, in-stock products. Do not bulk-transfer the old pub/media/catalog/product folder.

Migrate and map SEO URL Rewrites for this active catalog.

STEP 9: Marketing Tracking, Final Performance Tuning & Go-Live Testing

Verify frontend/backend event dispatching maps exactly to original setup (Data layers: view_item, add_to_cart, purchase). Activate production mode, Varnish FPC, Redis caching, and execute JS/CSS optimizations. Perform full end-to-end sandbox checkout walkthroughs on both store views.

Nobody is forced to accept a project they do not believe in. A professional always has the right to decline if the budget, scope, or timeline does not align with their expectations. A true professional understands that software engineering is not only about writing code — it is also about character, planning, discipline, ownership, and respect for the client who is investing trust, time, and financial resources into the collaboration.

What we value most is simple:

Job Description:

We are looking for a highly skilled Adobe Commerce (Magento 2) Solutions Architect/Developer to execute a clean-start rebuild of our e-commerce platform. We require a professional to build a robust, optimized, and scalable environment from scratch.

Technical Roadmap & Project Scope:

STEP 1: Fresh Baseline & Clean Magento 2.4.8 Installation
Technical Execution: Set up a completely isolated, clean database and environment on the new staging directory. Install a pristine baseline of Magento 2.4.8 core cleanly via Composer. Do not copy, migrate, or reuse any existing core files from the old server setup.

Core Optimization & Regional Clean-up: We sell exclusively to customers in Romania and Europe. To make the platform as lightweight as possible, please disable the default Magento core modules and background loops that strictly target the American or Asian market infrastructures. This includes: Vertex, Amazon Pay, Braintree/PayPal core modules (non-European configurations), Yotpo, Dotdigital, and default US/Global Shipping Carriers. Identify and disable any other default core modules that strictly target non-European configurations.

Core Server Engines & Caching Stack Infrastructure:

Install and configure separate, dedicated Redis instances (one for backend session handling, one for default application caching).

Install OpenSearch 2.x and map it as the primary catalog search engine.

Install and configure Varnish for Full Page Cache (FPC).

Critical: Varnish must be completely bypassed / turned OFF during the entire development and configuration phase.

STEP 3: Official Theme Installation & Visual Brand Alignment
Perform a 100% clean installation of the official MGS Claue (Parent) theme, followed by our customized Child Theme. Strict Rebranding Rule: Rename the child theme folder to "deepinvogue" and ensure all text fields and store names in the configuration reflect DeepInVogue. No code logic changes should be made to the theme files.

STEP 4: Native Magento Dual-Store Architecture Setup
Create a clean, dual-store view hierarchy under the main website bucket:

Store View 1: Romania (Base Currency: RON / Default Language: RO).

Store View 2: International (Base Currency: EUR / Default Language: EN).

Critical: Store codes and structural IDs must match our original live site exactly to maintain GTM/Facebook CAPI data integrity.

STEP 5: Core Extensions Installation & PHP 8.3 Compatibility Audit
Deploy operational extensions (GeoIP Store Switcher, Currency Switcher, Infinite Scroll, One Step Checkout, PayU Payment Gateway, Discount Module). Audit each for 100% stable execution under PHP 8.3. Run full compilation and static content deployment; monitor terminal logs for any PHP 8.3 deprecation notices or layout XML conflicts.

STEP 6: Extension Configuration & Checkout Optimization Strategy
Replicate exact configuration paths from our live site for extensions. Configure currency automated cron jobs. Replicate our simplified, fields-reduced checkout setup exactly; this requires our close, mutual consultation.

STEP 7: Relational Data Migration (The Clean Database Principle)
Perform highly selective, isolated relational data migration from the old database into our fresh, clean Magento 2.4.x structure, maintaining perfect relational integrity for:

Customers & Customer Groups.

Order History, Invoices, & Shipments.

Critical: Relational keys must remain perfectly intact.

STEP 8: Filtered Product Catalog & Clean Media Asset Import

Filter product catalog to include ONLY active, in-stock products.

Critical Media Rule: Migrate and map ONLY the images belonging to active, in-stock products. Do not bulk-transfer the old pub/media/catalog/product folder.

Migrate and map SEO URL Rewrites for this active catalog.

STEP 9: Marketing Tracking, Final Performance Tuning & Go-Live Testing
Verify frontend/backend event dispatching maps exactly to original setup (Data layers: view_item, add_to_cart, purchase). Activate production mode, Varnish FPC, Redis caching, and execute JS/CSS optimizations. Perform full end-to-end sandbox checkout walkthroughs on both store views.

Professional Expectations & Zero-Tolerance Policy:

Values & Commitment: This project requires a mature, stoic, and fully accountable professional. We acknowledge that complex projects may involve unforeseen technical challenges; however, we are looking for a partner who takes full ownership and is willing to dedicate extra time if necessary to ensure success. We do not work with individuals who use a "victim mentality" or excuses for missed deadlines to justify demands for extra payment. We do not pay for errors that need to be fixed, nor do we look for professionals who create issues and then ask for money to resolve them. Such bad practices will be reported. Any such behavior will not be tolerated and will lead to the immediate termination of the project. If you view clients as a source of easy money to be exploited, we do not share the same values and this project is not for you.

Budget Integrity: We have calculated the time and budget carefully. We require a fixed price for the outlined scope. Any attempt to request a budget increase midway through the project because of a lack of proper analysis or a dishonest strategy to inflate costs will result in the immediate termination of the project, regardless of progress.

Passion vs. Profit: If you are here just for the money and lack the passion for high-quality engineering, please do not apply. This requirement, integrity, responsability and passion for work is the most important part of this project.

Requirements for the Applicant:

Proven experience with Magento 2.4.8 and PHP 8.3.

Strong DevOps skills (Linux, Redis, Varnish, OpenSearch).

Please outline your specific process for Step 7 (Selective Data Migration) and Step 8 (Media Filtering) in your proposal.

Inventory
Raw materials
Finished goods
BOMs
Workstations
Routings
Manufacturing orders
Production tracking
Purchasing needs
Costing
Finished goods handover
Our factory produces wigs, hairpieces, toppers, and related products. The production process involves multiple stages, material variations, and labor-intensive handwork.
MRPeasy will be used for factory operations only, not for B2C salon or retail customer management.
What We Need
We need someone who can help us:
Design the MRPeasy structure
Set up product groups and item/SKU logic
Set up raw materials and finished goods
Create BOM structures
Create routing and workstation structures
Set up customer/account logic
Set up vendor/supplier logic
Prepare data import templates
Support initial data cleanup and migration
Test one full production workflow
Review costing and inventory logic
Document the setup

Our factory works with account customers. Each account may have its own end clients, but in MRPeasy we want to track the account customer, not every individual retail client.
Example:
MRPeasy Customer: Schöne Haare GmbH
End Client Reference: SCHOENE-2026-001
The goal is to keep MRPeasy clean and factory-focused.
Initial Deliverables
By the end of the first phase, we expect:
1. MRPeasy structure proposal
2. Product group and item/SKU structure
3. Initial material master setup
4. Initial customer/account setup
5. Initial vendor/supplier setup

12. Import-ready templates for future data entry

The ideal candidate has experience with:
MRPeasy implementation
Manufacturing ERP/MRP setup
Inventory structure
BOM design
Production routing
Workstations
Manufacturing orders
CSV import / data migration
Factory workflow mapping
Material costing
MRPeasy experience is strongly preferred. Experience with similar systems such as Odoo Manufacturing, Katana, Fishbowl, NetSuite, Cin7, SAP Business One, or other MRP/ERP systems may also be acceptable.
Project Details
Project type: Hourly or milestone-based contract
Initial budget: $3,000 USD
Project focus: MRPeasy setup and factory workflow implementation
Potential extension: Yes
Collaboration: High-touch guidance from our operations team
Suggested Milestones
Milestone 1: Discovery and MRPeasy structure design
Milestone 2: Master data framework and import templates
Milestone 3: BOM, workstation, and routing setup
Milestone 4: Full test production flow
Milestone 5: Documentation and handover

What would your first two weeks of work look like?

What jobs are open
Which account customer each job belongs to
What materials are needed
What materials are missing
What stage each job is in
What has been consumed
What has been finished
What each product costs
What needs to be purchased
What is ready for handover
We are looking for someone who can help us build a simple, clean, and scalable MRPeasy foundation for our factory.

upwork-vibe~upwork-job-scraper.title: Hands-On Ecommerce Operations Lead for Shopify Shipping, Fulfillment, 3PL, and Process Improvement
upwork-vibe~upwork-job-scraper.description:
We are looking for a hands-on Ecommerce Operations Lead to take ownership of our shipping and fulfillment function.

This is not a virtual assistant role. This is not a basic order processor role. This is also not a corporate manager role where you only supervise and talk strategy.

We need someone who can lead by doing.

The mission is simple: make sure every customer order either ships quickly or has a clear reason, owner, next action, and follow-up time. No silent pending orders.

We sell high-ticket electric scooters, electric bikes, parts, and accessories through Shopify. Our operation involves Shopify orders, 3PL coordination, warehouse follow-up, inventory blockers, customer update triggers, purchase order/inbound issues, and fulfillment exceptions.

The right person will own the daily shipping queue and improve the process while actively working inside the process. You should be comfortable jumping into Shopify, checking orders, following up with the warehouse or 3PL, identifying blockers, escalating when people do not reply, updating internal trackers, and sending clear reports to management.

We are not looking for someone passive. If an order is blocked, we do not want you to wait quietly. We want you to find out why, contact the right person, follow up, call if needed, escalate if needed, document the issue, and keep the order moving.

You will work closely with our inventory/supply chain person, who handles supplier availability, Stockie, POs, inbound inventory, and inventory accuracy. Your main lane is fulfillment speed, pending orders, 3PL/warehouse coordination, blocked-order ownership, customer update triggers, and shipping process improvement.

A normal day may include reviewing all pending Shopify orders, separating orders into ready-to-ship versus blocked, chasing warehouse or 3PL contacts for confirmation, identifying inventory mismatches, coordinating with inventory team on out-of-stock items, making sure customer support knows which customers need updates, flagging website/product availability issues, and sending a daily report showing what shipped, what is blocked, why it is blocked, who owns it, and what happens next.

The person we hire must be able to operate like an owner. We do not want someone who needs to be managed every hour. We want someone who naturally improves broken processes without waiting to be asked.

You must be hands-on. If the order queue is messy, you should be willing to jump in and clean it. If the tracker is missing, you should build it. If the warehouse is not replying, you should chase them. If a problem keeps repeating, you should recommend a process fix.

You are a strong fit if you have experience in ecommerce operations, Shopify fulfillment, 3PL coordination, warehouse operations, order management, shipping operations, process improvement, SOP creation, or fulfillment exception management.

You are also a strong fit if you have used tools like Shopify, ShipStation, ShipHero, Stockie, Cin7, Finale Inventory, SKULabs, Unleashed, NetSuite, Airtable, Google Sheets, Gorgias, or similar ecommerce operations tools.

You are not a fit if your experience is mostly customer support, simple order processing, data entry, or following SOPs that someone else already built.

You are not a fit if you wait passively for replies, need perfect instructions for every step, dislike messy operations, avoid chasing people, or only want to manage from a distance.

We care about speed, ownership, clarity, and follow-through. We do not care about fancy corporate language. We need someone who can reduce daily fires and make the operation run without the founder constantly checking every detail.

The goal of this role is that after 30 days, the founder should not need to ask why orders are not shipping. You should already know, already have the blocker categorized, already have the owner assigned, and already have the next action in motion.

Every pending order should move toward one of these outcomes: shipped, confirmed preorder ETA, customer decision, substitute item, cancellation/refund, or clear escalation.

If you are the type of person who sees a messy process and immediately wants to fix it, this role may be a good fit.

If you are the type of person who waits for someone else to tell you exactly what to do, this role is not a good fit.

To apply, please answer the screening questions carefully. Generic answers such as “I will coordinate with the team” or “I am detail-oriented” will not be considered.
questions: It is 10AM, shipping cutoff is 2PM, and 23 Shopify orders are pending. Some are ready, some blocked. What do you do first?
You messaged the warehouse about a blocked order 45 minutes ago and got no reply. Shipping cutoff is soon. What do you do next?
Are you better at following existing SOPs or building/fixing messy processes while doing the work? Give a real example.
After 30 days in this role, what should the boss no longer need to manage or chase you about?
Tell me about a process you personally improved without being asked. What was broken, what did you change, and what was the result?

upwork-vibe~upwork-job-scraper.title: Cross-Platform Body-Composition Analysis Platform
upwork-vibe~upwork-job-scraper.description:
Project summary
We are commissioning the development of a professional-use software platform for body-composition analysis from photographic input. The platform is composed of three deliverables that work together:
1.	A desktop application (macOS + Windows) — the practitioner's primary working environment. Holds all client records, sessions, photos, results, and trends locally.
2.	A cross-platform mobile application (iOS + Android) — a single binary, published to App Store and Google Play, with two runtime modes (professional mode and end-user mode).
3.	A lightweight backend — handles licensing, a transient analysis API, and two encrypted relay services for device-to-device photo transfer.
The platform replaces an existing web-based product. Migration tooling for existing customer data is part of scope.
Mandatory technical constraints
•	Frontend / clients: Flutter for all three client targets (desktop and mobile). A single codebase strategy is expected where reasonable; platform-specific code only where Flutter's cross-platform capabilities fall short.
•	Backend: open — the bidder proposes the stack. Constraints: must support standard REST/WebSocket APIs, encrypted blob storage with strict retention limits, and a license/quota enforcement layer. Examples we are open to: Xano, Supabase, custom Node/Go/Python on managed infrastructure. Justify the choice in the proposal.
•	Continuous integration: open, but the desktop pipeline must handle macOS notarization and Windows code signing end-to-end. Codemagic, GitHub Actions with self-hosted runners, or equivalent are all acceptable.
•	Source control: Git (provider open). Repositories provided by us.
•	Camera + pose validation: Google ML Kit Pose Detection (existing reference implementation in our current mobile codebase can be reused as a starting point).
Component specifications
1. Desktop application (macOS + Windows)
Purpose: practitioner's primary tool. Holds all client and session data on the practitioner's local machine — there is no cloud-side data repository for client records.
Required features:
•	Authentication / license activation. First launch flow: license key entered once, validated against the backend, then revalidated periodically online with an offline grace period.
•	Client records. Full CRUD on a client list with profile fields, search, sorting, and a required client-typology enum field (final values to be supplied; conceptual model is a 7-category framing such as standard / lean / athletic / muscular / overweight / category-A obese / category-B obese).
•	Folders / sessions. Hierarchical organization of client sessions, each containing one or more analyses.
•	Analysis capture. Import a photo from a local file picker; the desktop calls the analysis API with the photo + client typology, receives a JSON measurement payload, and persists it alongside the photo.
•	Analysis detail view. Charts (trend over time, current snapshot), per-measurement breakdown, references to standardised reference tables.
•	Local encrypted persistence. SQLite for structured data, encrypted on disk; photos stored in an encrypted local directory. Encryption keys derived from the user session.
•	Backup and export. Full archive (database + photos) exported as a single signed file. Optional backup destination: a user-chosen filesystem folder (no cloud SDKs to implement — if the user picks a folder inside their personal iCloud Drive / OneDrive / Google Drive / Dropbox, the OS handles sync).
•	Import. Restore from a backup archive; also import from the legacy-platform export format (specification to be provided).
•	Auto-update. Direct distribution (not via app stores). macOS uses Sparkle; Windows uses WinSparkle, Squirrel.Windows, or MSIX App Installer — bidder proposes. Appcast-style version manifest hosted on our infrastructure. Stable + opt-in beta channels. Rollback via appcast revision.
•	Code signing and notarization. Apple Developer ID + notarization on macOS; EV Code Signing Certificate on Windows. Full integration into the CI pipeline.
•	Onboarding stack. First-launch acceptance of disclaimers and references to standardised classification tables (exact copy to be supplied). Version-gated; reshown when content version increments.
•	Visual design. Modern, professional aesthetic. A design discovery phase precedes Phase 2 build. Component-level redesign (cards, tables, charts, form controls) over the existing flows — flows themselves remain familiar to current users.
•	Crash and metadata telemetry. Sentry or equivalent. No client-data exfiltration in telemetry payloads.
2. Mobile application (iOS + Android)
Single binary, published once to App Store and Google Play. Two modes selected at runtime based on activation method.
Professional mode
•	Unlocked by pairing with a desktop: the desktop shows a QR code containing its public key and a session token; the mobile scans it, exchanges keys, and stores the pairing in secure storage.
•	Reuses the existing pose-validation pipeline from our current mobile app (camera + pose detectors + tilt feedback + real-time guidance).
•	After capture: transfers the photo to the paired desktop via the most efficient available path:
o	LAN transport when both devices are on the same network: an HTTPS server on the desktop with mDNS / Bonjour advertisement, TLS via a self-signed cert pinned at pairing time, multipart POST upload.
o	Same-user encrypted relay as fallback when LAN discovery fails: the mobile encrypts the photo with the desktop's public key and uploads ciphertext to a backend relay endpoint; the desktop subscribes and pulls.
•	The hybrid logic attempts mDNS for ~1-2 seconds; if a paired desktop is reachable on LAN, uses LAN, otherwise falls back to relay.
•	No persistent storage of captures on the mobile device — photos are transferred and discarded.
End-user mode (code-gated)
•	Unlocked per session by entering a session code issued by a professional from the desktop application. No account, no signup, no persisted PII.
•	The session code is a QR (the desktop displays it on-screen for in-person use, or exports it as an image for remote sharing). The mobile reads the QR from the live camera or from an image in the device's photo library (both iOS Vision and Android ML Kit support QR-from-image natively).
•	After capture: the mobile encrypts the photo with the professional's public key (fetched from the relay via session ID) before any bytes leave the device, then uploads ciphertext to a cross-user relay endpoint.
•	The desktop receives the ciphertext, decrypts with its private key, shows the professional a preview for visual confirmation, and on accept imports the photo into the corresponding client record.
•	Session properties:
o	The professional chooses one-shot (closes after first successful upload) or persistent-per-client (multiple uploads over a longer window, bound to a specific client record).
o	One-shot TTL is professional-configurable: 24h / 48h / 7d, default 48h.
o	Persistent codes have a longer or configurable TTL.
o	The professional can revoke any active code from the desktop at any time.
•	First-use disclosure screen explaining what is sent, that the platform operator cannot read the contents, and the metadata retention window. Exact copy supplied later.
Shared mobile concerns
•	Strip the current mobile codebase down to: camera + pose validators + mode router + transport layer + minimal settings.
•	Reuse the existing pose-validation pipeline (suite of validators in our current codebase: arms, feet, hands, profile, static pose, tilt control). Code can be adopted as-is or refactored.
•	Visual design aligned with the desktop refresh (parallel design workstream).
•	Public App Store and Google Play publication, including all store-listing assets, privacy manifests, and review submissions.
3. Backend
Minimal scope. Bidder proposes the stack. Required services:
•	License server.
o	User accounts for professionals (email + auth).
o	Four license SKU shapes from day one: monthly subscription, annual subscription, lifetime one-time, multi-seat practice pack with shared billing.
o	Desktop activation flow + offline grace period.
o	Free-trial issuance with two concurrent limits (time-based + analysis-count-based), with both limits configurable per individual new user so sales can tune trial generosity case-by-case.
o	Billing integration: Stripe (or equivalent) for cards, plus support for invoice/bank-transfer manual flows.
•	Analysis API gateway.
o	Desktop authenticates with a license-bound session token; the backend verifies license validity + remaining quota before forwarding the request to an existing third-party analysis service (URL and contract provided).
o	Stateless and transient: no retention of image bytes; no logging of image content; metadata logging only (timestamp, license ID, response code, compute time).
o	Pass-through: receives image + client-typology enum from the desktop, calls the upstream service, returns the JSON payload.
•	Same-user encrypted relay.
o	Session creation by desktop, session resolution by the paired mobile, ciphertext upload, ciphertext stream subscription by desktop (long-lived authenticated WebSocket).
o	No persistence of ciphertext past session end. No logging of body content.
•	Cross-user encrypted relay (end-user mode → professional desktop).
o	Session creation by desktop with reusability flag (one-shot or persistent-per-client) and configurable TTL.
o	Session resolution by mobile in end-user mode.
o	Ciphertext upload, ciphertext stream subscription by desktop.
o	Revocation endpoint for the desktop.
o	Operational caps (per-image size, per-license session creation rate) configurable in backend settings, adjustable post-launch without a client release.
o	Metadata retention: 30 days (session ID, timestamps, source IP, image size, license ID). Zero retention of ciphertext content past session end.
•	Auto-update metadata.
o	Static version-manifest endpoints for desktop and mobile auto-updaters.
o	Separate stable and beta channels for desktop.
•	Admin / operations console.
o	Internal-only UI to: issue and revoke licenses, set trial limits, view (metadata-only) usage and session telemetry, push announcements.
o	Authentication: separate admin role, MFA required.
4. Migration tooling
•	A one-time data exporter on the existing legacy platform (specifications and access provided) that produces per-professional archives containing their full client data, sessions, photos, and history.
•	A corresponding importer in the desktop application that reconstructs the local database and file layout from those archives.
•	Parallel-run period during which both platforms remain operational; specifics handled commercially, not part of the development quote.
Non-functional requirements
Supported platforms
•	macOS: latest two major releases plus the two prior, x86_64 + Apple Silicon.
•	Windows: Windows 10 (1809+) and Windows 11, x86_64. ARM64 desirable but not required.
•	iOS: the latest version and the two prior majors.
•	Android: API level 26 (Android 8.0) and above.
Performance
•	Desktop cold-launch under 3 seconds on a 2020-era machine.
•	Mobile camera-to-capture latency under 200 ms.
•	Pose-validation feedback rendered at the camera preview frame rate (target 30 fps; minimum 20 fps on lower-end Android devices).
•	Local DB queries return within 100 ms for typical paginated lists (up to 5000 client records).
•	Auto-update check completes in the background without blocking app startup.
Security baseline
•	All network communication over TLS.
•	Local data at rest encrypted with platform-provided keychains (macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager, iOS Keychain, Android Keystore).
•	End-to-end encrypted relays use asymmetric crypto; bidder proposes the specific scheme (e.g. X25519 for key exchange, XChaCha20-Poly1305 or AES-256-GCM for payload encryption, Ed25519 for signatures).
•	No third-party SDK that exfiltrates user content (no analytics SDKs that record screen contents; no SDKs that upload arbitrary data).
•	Auto-updaters verify cryptographic signatures on every package before installation (Sparkle EdDSA on macOS; equivalent on Windows).
Testing
•	Unit tests for core business logic (license validation, encryption helpers, pagination state, validator pipeline).
•	Widget tests for critical UI flows (login, capture, results display).
•	Integration tests for the LAN transport path and the relay fallback path.
•	Manual QA checklist covering: pairing flows, code generation and redemption, all transport paths, offline / online transitions, license expiry behaviour, auto-update across one version bump.
Internationalisation
•	English and Italian at launch. Further languages addable without code changes (ARB-based localisation, established convention).
•	All user-facing strings externalised. No hardcoded copy.
Integration points
The bidder will need to integrate with:
•	Existing third-party body-composition analysis service — URL and API contract provided. Treat as a black box; the new backend proxies to it.
•	Apple Developer Program account (we provide credentials) for macOS signing + notarization and iOS publication.
•	Microsoft Partner / EV Code Signing Certificate (we provide; bidder proposes vendor — DigiCert, Sectigo, GlobalSign, SSL.com, K-Software are all acceptable).
•	Google Play Console account (we provide).
•	Apple App Store Connect account (we provide).
•	Sentry (or equivalent crash-reporting) — we provide the workspace.
•	Stripe (or equivalent payment provider) — we provide the account; bidder configures the integration.
•	A CDN / object-storage provider for hosting installer packages and appcast feeds — bidder proposes (Cloudflare R2, AWS S3 + CloudFront, Bunny, etc.).
Phasing
We expect quotes in five phases. The phases can overlap where dependencies allow.
1.	Backend foundations. License server with all four SKU shapes, trial mechanism, analysis-API gateway with quota enforcement, encrypted-relay endpoint contracts, auto-update manifest endpoints.
2.	Desktop application MVP. Full feature parity with the existing professional web workflow, plus the new local-only data model, backup/export, auto-update, and code signing.
3.	Mobile application — both modes. Pose-validation refactor, professional-mode pairing, end-user-mode code-redemption, LAN transport, App Store + Play Store submission.
4.	Encrypted relays. Same-user and cross-user relay implementations, end-to-end key exchange, session lifecycle, monitoring and abnormal-pattern alerting.
5.	Legacy migration tooling. Exporter for the legacy platform, importer in the desktop application, end-to-end migration smoke test on real customer data.
The bidder may propose a different phase split if technically justified.
Quote structure
We expect the proposal to include:
1.	Team composition — named roles, seniority, fractional vs full-time, who works on which phase. Flutter desktop experience is required for the team lead.
2.	Per-phase cost breakdown — total effort (person-days) and price per phase.
3.	Timeline per phase — start date, duration, target completion. Identify dependencies and critical path.
4.	Recurring infrastructure cost estimate — what the platform will cost to run after launch, broken down by category (object storage, CDN, backend hosting, code-signing certs, developer-program memberships). We accept ranges.
5.	Backend stack recommendation with rationale — why this stack, with operating cost and operational complexity considered.
6.	Auto-updater proposal for Windows (since this is the most open of the platform choices).
7.	Risk register — what could go wrong in each phase, mitigation approach.
8.	Acceptance criteria — what "done" looks like for each phase. We will negotiate.
9.	Warranty and post-launch support terms — bug-fix coverage period, response SLAs for the first 90 days.
10.	Prior work — at least two prior Flutter desktop apps you've shipped to production, with public references or demo access where possible.
Selection criteria
In approximate order of weight:
1.	Demonstrable Flutter desktop production experience (macOS + Windows with signing and auto-update — not just mobile Flutter).
2.	End-to-end encryption / secure-channel design experience.
3.	Cross-platform CI maturity, especially for the macOS + Windows signing pipeline.
4.	Backend pragmatism — preference for stacks the team has actually shipped, not the newest thing.
5.	Communication quality during the bidding conversation (clear questions back, no hand-waving).
6.	Total cost, weighted against credibility of the timeline.
What we provide
•	Existing mobile codebase (Flutter, ~30k lines) as a starting reference, particularly for the pose-validation pipeline.
•	Existing legacy web platform access for the migration exporter work.
•	All cloud accounts, developer-program memberships, and certificates listed under "Integration points".
•	Design assets / brand guidance, available after kickoff.
•	Final reference-table sources and exact disclaimer copy (delivered before Phase 2 build starts).
Out of scope for this quotation
•	Marketing site.
•	Customer support tooling beyond the internal admin console.
•	iOS-side local inference (planned as a follow-up track after this engagement closes).
•	Linux desktop port (may be commissioned later if customer demand emerges).
•	Production hosting fees and certificate purchases (we cover these directly).
How to apply
Process gate. A complete written cost and effort estimate is mandatory before any shortlist or technical call. We will not schedule a synchronous conversation or shortlist your application until we have received an estimate that covers the full scope of this document.
Written clarification questions are welcome at any time, including before you submit your estimate. Send them in writing; we answer in writing, and we share the questions and answers with every active bidder so the information field stays level. Do not let a missing detail block you from asking — better to ask than to discover an assumption mid-build.
What we do not do at the pre-estimate stage: live calls, voice or video meetings, demo sessions, or any other synchronous exchange. Those are reserved for shortlisted bidders after the estimate has been reviewed.
The estimate must include:
•	Per-phase effort (person-days) and price, broken down as described under "Quote structure".
•	A single total price for the whole engagement.
•	Timeline per phase, including critical-path dependencies.
•	Assumptions the estimate relies on. We will challenge or accept these in writing; once accepted, they become contractual.
Estimate-vs-actual policy. The accepted estimate is a soft cap. We will accept overruns up to +20-25% without renegotiation, provided they are flagged with a written justification before the cost is incurred. Any overrun beyond that buffer requires explicit prior approval and may trigger a scope or price review. Estimates that prove materially under-scoped (more than 25% overrun without prior justification) will affect milestone payments and our willingness to continue the engagement.
You are encouraged to inflate the estimate to reflect honest uncertainty — a higher estimate with a comfortable buffer is preferable to a low estimate with constant overruns. Sandbagging is fine; chronic re-estimating is not.
Process flow.
1.	Read this document. Ask any written questions you need to size the work confidently.
2.	Submit a complete estimate per the format above.
3.	We review the estimate against the spec.
4.	Bidders whose estimates pass review are invited to a 60-minute technical conversation.
5.	Award within 2-3 weeks of receiving acceptable estimates. Work starts shortly after.

upwork-vibe~upwork-job-scraper.description:
Title: AWS Architect — Design Multi-Tenant OpenClaw Deployment (Greenfield Project)
Category: IT & Networking → DevOps & Solution Architecture
Engagement: Fixed-price project
Experience level: Expert
Estimated budget: $X,XXX (open to proposals)
Timeline: X weeks

Project summary
Design a greenfield, cloud-native, multi-tenant OpenClaw deployment on AWS (or comparable cloud — GCP / Azure proposals welcome with justification). The goal is an architecture that can host multiple isolated OpenClaw gateways per customer, with hard isolation of compute, secrets, state, and network across tenants.
Design-first project. Strong delivery may lead to a follow-on implementation project.
Why this project is interesting

True greenfield — no legacy migration, design it the right way from day one
Real multi-tenancy problem: credential bleed, blast radius, per-tenant IAM, network isolation
Direct collaboration with the founder — fast decisions, no committee
Designed for production from the start, not a proof-of-concept
Clear scope, clear deliverables, clean handoff

Scope of work
Design a cloud-native multi-tenant OpenClaw platform covering:

Tenancy model — silo vs pool vs bridge, with a strong opinion on which fits OpenClaw and why
Per-tenant gateway isolation: separate compute, IAM roles, secrets, state
Secrets architecture using AWS Secrets Manager / Parameter Store (or equivalent), with a clean per-tenant naming convention
Compute strategy for gateway processes — ECS, Fargate, EKS, EC2+systemd, or other — with justification
Network isolation between tenants (VPC, subnet, SG, or account-level boundaries)
State storage strategy per tenant (EFS, EBS, S3, or managed alternatives) with appropriate locking and durability
Port management and service discovery across multiple gateways per tenant (OpenClaw uses base, base+2, base+3)
Channel token discipline aligned with OpenClaw conventions (tokens in accounts only)
Tenant lifecycle: provisioning, upgrading, decommissioning, disaster recovery
Deployment pipeline (Terraform, CDK, Pulumi, or equivalent IaC)
Observability: per-tenant log isolation, metrics, alerting
Cost model — what does each tenant cost at idle and at load
Compatibility with the cc-openclaw Claude Code skills ecosystem

Deliverables

Architecture diagrams — component, network, IAM/secrets flow, tenant lifecycle
Design doc covering tenancy model, tradeoffs, and decision rationale
IaC scaffold (Terraform, CDK, or Pulumi) for one tenant, plus the replication pattern
Tenant provisioning runbook
Disaster recovery and tenant offboarding runbook
Cost-per-tenant model with assumptions documented

Required expertise

OpenClaw gateway internals: OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH, OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR, port behavior, channel/account config, pairing state
Claude Code skills, including familiarity with the cc-openclaw repo
AWS (or equivalent cloud): VPC design, IAM least-privilege, secrets management, container/compute orchestration, managed storage, observability stack
Multi-tenant SaaS patterns — silo vs pool vs bridge — with shipped experience
Terraform, CDK, or Pulumi in production
Credential isolation and blast radius design

Bonus

Telegram / Slack / WhatsApp bot operations at scale
Prior cloud-native agent infrastructure
Security background (IAM hardening, secret rotation, audit trails, SOC 2 readiness)
Cost optimization for multi-tenant workloads

Team or solo
Open to either. Small teams welcome — if you're a 2–3 person shop with complementary skills (architect + IaC engineer + security), say so and include the team's breakdown.
Screening questions — please answer in your proposal

Silo, pool, or bridge tenancy model for OpenClaw — pick one and defend it.
How would you prevent credential bleed across tenants? Be concrete about the cloud primitives.
Compute layer for the gateway processes — what's your pick and why?
Link to a comparable multi-tenant cloud platform you've shipped.
One thing about OpenClaw's flat-file, gateway-per-tier model that's hard to do cleanly in the cloud, and how you'd handle it.

How to stand out
Short proposals beat long ones. Skip the boilerplate intro. Lead with your answers to questions 1 and 5 — that's the signal I'm reading for.

upwork-vibe~upwork-job-scraper.title: Part-Time Full-Stack Developer — Platform Migration & Ongoing Technical Support
upwork-vibe~upwork-job-scraper.description:
About the Company

We're an early-stage AI-powered SaaS platform in the financial services space. We're live, we have active users, a pipeline in motion, and we're moving fast. We're not looking for someone to help us figure out what to build. We know what we're building. We need someone to help us build it on an infrastructure that can actually support it.

What We Need

We're migrating off Replit onto a production-grade stack, Supabase (Postgres), Railway (backend and API server), and Vercel (frontend), and we need a developer who can execute that migration cleanly, get everything stable, and then stay on part-time to handle the technical work that comes with scaling a live platform.

We're looking for someone sharp, autonomous, and reliable, someone who can take a well-documented plan and run with it.

The Migration Scope (Phase 1 Project)

- Export and restore a full Postgres database (490K+ records, 117 tables) from Replit into Supabase, verified and clean
- Deploy the backend API and MCP server as separate services on Railway.
- Migrate the frontend to Vercel, connected to the Railway backend.
- Migrate all background and scheduled jobs to Railway workers.
- Set up all environment variables and confirm all services are communicating correctly. 
- Fix several known MCP tool issues from wrong table references, missing error handling, query timeouts, and new diagnostic tooling.
- Confirm full end-to-end functionality before decommissioning Replit

Ongoing Retainer (After Migration)
A few hours per week as needed for:

- Debugging production issues when they arise
- Railway and Supabase configuration as the platform evolves
Database performance, indexing and query optimization as data grows.
- Supporting new feature development that requires real engineering work.
- Being a reliable technical resource when something breaks and needs real eyes on it.

Who You Are

- Excellent with Node.js or Python on the backend.  You've built and deployed real APIs.
- Comfortable with Postgres. You can write clean SQL, understand indexing, and read a query plan
- Have deployed on Railway, Render, or similar.  You're not learning the platform on our dime.
- Have worked with Supabase or can get up to speed quickly.
- Understand MCP (Model Context Protocol) or are willing to get familiar with it. Our Claude integration is a core part of the platform.
- You communicate proactively. If something is going to take longer than expected, you say so before the deadline, not after.
- You work well alongside a non-technical founder who moves fast and makes decisions quickly.

Nice to Have

- Experience with data-heavy platforms at scale
- Familiarity with AI tooling, agents, or LLM integrations
- Experience with financial data pipelines or large third-party data feeds

What This Is Not

This is not a role for someone who needs hand-holding or detailed specs written for every task. The migration plan is documented and thorough. We need someone who can read it, ask the right clarifying questions, and execute. If you've never independently deployed a production application, this isn't the right fit.

How to Apply
Send a brief note, not a template, an actual note covering:

1. A project you've migrated or deployed that's similar in scope to what's described here
2. Your experience with Postgres at scale and any of the platforms mentioned. Railway, Supabase, Vercel
3. Your availability and typical weekly capacity
4. Your rate for the initial migration project and your preferred retainer structure

**Applications without a genuine response to all four points won't be reviewed**
